text:
Anya: FYI I hit a weird correctness blip when enabling the new INT4 attention kernel behind the feature flag — sequences with KV stride != 1 sometimes produce garbled tokens.
Dmitri: ugh. do you have a minimal repro? seq len / batch / model? :thinking:
Anya: repro: seq=1024, batch=2, kv_stride=2 after concat transform (old export). Happens only when kernel path uses packed layout. smaller seqs are fine.
Kevin M: is this a layout mismatch (export vs kernel expectation) or a math/quant rounding bug?
Anya: looks like layout mismatch. kernel assumes contiguous packing per head; export used interleaved channels for historical reasons. INT8/INT4 kernels do much tighter packing so they expose the mismatch.
Hafsa: two immediate options: 1) shim at runtime that remaps strides to the kernel expectation (adapter), 2) change exporter to normalize layout and ship a model conversion step (breaking change). Both have tradeoffs.
Dmitri: adapter seems safest short-term to avoid breaking customer exports. perf hit? small mem copy maybe but we can make it zero-copy for common cases.
Kevin M: we should also consider an ABI/handshake: kernel registry should advertise supported KV layouts and an auto-fallback to fp16/INT8 path if adapter not allowed. explicit opt-in for adapter via flag.
Anya: prototype of registry check I sketched:
```
// kernel_meta.h
struct KernelMeta { string name; vector<string> supported_kv_layouts; bool prefers_packed; };
registry.register({"attn_int4_v1", {"packed_per_head","contig_head"}, true});
```
Dmitri: perfect. runtime can pick first compatible or insert a layout_adapter op. keep the adapter as a small transform op in the graph so we can trace it and measure.
Hafsa: rollout plan: canary on dedicated pool -> perf + correctness harness -> small user-facing opt-in flag `runtime.flags.enable_lowprec_kv_adapter` -> then gradual auto-enable if no regressions.
Anya: CI output from earlier run (trimmed):
```
rilly-bot: canary-run 1718204800: 1024-seq-int4-attn: correctness=FAIL (mismatch at token 17)
ci-bot: canary-run 1718204860: adapter-enabled: correctness=PASS, p99 latency +3%
```
Kevin M: +3% p99 is acceptable for now if it fixes correctness. we can optimize adapter later (vectorized copy, chunked async copies).
Dmitri: long-term we should add a model-level KV_LAYOUT tag in the model manifest so exporter explicitly states layout. then kernel selection is deterministic. also add a 'compat_version' so old runtimes refuse unknown formats.
Hafsa: agree. action items:
- Anya: open PR with registry check + adapter op prototype (target: WIP by EOD)
- Dmitri: add tests to microbench harness for odd strides and seq boundaries
- Kevin M: measure perf of adapter variants (memcpy vs in-place remap)
- Hafsa: draft canary plan and flag names in ops doc
Anya: quick question — do we want adapter default OFF and opt-in via flag, or default ON with conservative fallback?
Dmitri: default OFF. opt-in gives us explicit control and avoids surprising perf regressions for users on older exporters. we can later flip default after 2 weeks of canary.
Hafsa: I'll schedule the canary and add a regression alert rule in console: if correctness drops or quality-signal < threshold -> autoscale rollback.
Anya: thanks all. I'll include a small eval prompt set to catch token drift at boundary cases.
Kevin M: nice. leave a clear TODO in PR for adding manifest KV_LAYOUT and compat_version.
Dmitri: and document the runtime flag in ops/flags.md.
rilly-bot: created issue #4021: "kv-layout adapter + kernel registry compatibility"
ci-bot: linked PR 7789 to issue #4021
Anya: closing loop here — ping me on PR comments for quick reviews :pray:
